title: Strings
summary: Palindromes, sliding window, expand around centre, minimum window

guide.title: Text is everywhere
points: Names, messages, URLs, logs and code itself are strings. Interviewers love string questions because they test careful indexing.
Palindromes, anagrams and "longest substring" questions appear in almost every company set.

guide.title: Where string skills are used
points: Search boxes and autocomplete match what you type against stored text.
Form validation: PAN, IFSC, e-mail and phone formats are string checks.
Spell check and plagiarism tools compare texts; genome tools search patterns in DNA strings (A, C, G, T).
Search result snippets highlight the shortest part of a page that contains all your words: the "minimum window" problem.

guide.title: A sequence of characters
points: A string works like an array of characters: s[i] is one character, length is the count.
In JavaScript, Java and Python strings cannot be changed in place; build a new one (or an array / StringBuilder) instead. C++ std::string can be changed.
Characters have codes: "a" is 97. Subtract "a" to map letters to 0–25 for counting.

code.python:
s = 'campus'
rev = s[::-1]
for ch in s:
    pass  # one character
print(len(s), rev, s[0])   # 6 supmac c

guide.title: Two pointers for palindromes
points: Compare the first and last characters, then move both inwards. Stop at the first mismatch.
O(n) time and no extra memory; clean the text first if case and punctuation should be ignored.

code.python:
l, r, ok = 0, len(s) - 1, True
while l < r:
    if s[l] != s[r]:
        ok = False
        break
    l += 1
    r -= 1

guide.title: Sliding window on text
points: Move the right edge to take a character in; move the left edge while the window breaks the rule (a repeat, a missing letter).
A map of counts or last positions tells you when the window is valid. Each character enters and leaves once: O(n).
Expand around the centre: every palindrome grows from a centre, so try all 2n − 1 centres for the longest one.

code.python:
# longest substring without repeating characters
last, l, best = {}, 0, 0
for r, ch in enumerate(s):
    if last.get(ch, -1) >= l:
        l = last[ch] + 1
    last[ch] = r
    best = max(best, r - l + 1)

guide.title: What breaks string code
points: Building a string with += in a loop: O(n²) in Java. Use StringBuilder (Java) or collect pieces and join.
Java: compare strings with equals(), never ==.
Upper and lower case are different characters; spaces and punctuation count too.
substring / slice end index is exclusive: s.substring(1, 3) has 2 characters.

guide.title: For advanced learners and interviews
points: Ask about the character set first: lowercase only (use a 26-size array), ASCII, or Unicode?
Pattern search: KMP and the Z-function find a pattern in O(n + m); rolling hashes (Rabin-Karp) compare substrings in O(1).
Longest palindromic substring in O(n) exists (Manacher), but expand-around-centre O(n²) is what interviews expect.
Next step: Hashing, which makes "have I seen this?" instant.

problems.title: Count the vowels
problems.statement: Return how many vowels (a, e, i, o, u in either case) the string has.

problems.title: Reverse the words
problems.statement: Return the words of the sentence in reverse order, separated by single spaces.
problems.hint: Split on spaces and drop empty pieces.

problems.title: Valid palindrome
problems.statement: Considering only letters and digits and ignoring case, return true if the string is a palindrome.
problems.hint: Remove other characters, then use two pointers.

problems.title: Anagram check
problems.statement: Return true if b is a rearrangement of the letters of a (exact characters).
problems.hint: Count characters, or sort both strings.

problems.title: Longest substring without repeats
problems.statement: Return the length of the longest substring with no repeated character.
problems.hint: Remember the last position of each character and move the left edge past it.

problems.title: Longest palindromic substring
problems.statement: Return the longest substring that is a palindrome. If there are several of that length, return the one that starts first.

problems.title: Count palindromic substrings
problems.statement: Return how many substrings are palindromes. Substrings at different positions count separately.
problems.hint: Every successful expansion step is one more palindrome.

problems.title: Minimum window substring
problems.statement: Return the shortest substring of s that contains every character of t (with repeats). Print NONE if there is none. If several are shortest, return the leftmost.
problems.hint: Count what is still missing; shrink the window whenever nothing is missing.
